title.en: Você, o senhor, and a senhora

summary.en: Everyday Brazilian Portuguese uses você with peers and o senhor or a senhora for warm, respectful address.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 1.

In the kitchen, Camila asks Bianca *Aqui a gente fala você com todo mundo?* and Bianca replies: *Comigo, sempre! Deixe o senhor e a senhora para os hóspedes.* Soon after, when Jorge carries Dona Helena's heavy bag, he says *Eu vou levar a mala azul para a senhora*.

Across most of Brazil, *você* is the friendly everyday singular 'you' among coworkers, friends, and neighbors. When speaking respectfully to older adults or guesthouse visitors, Brazilians switch to *o senhor* (for a man) and *a senhora* (for a woman), or place *Seu* and *Dona* before a first name.

Best of all for learners, *você*, *o senhor*, and *a senhora* all take the exact same third-person singular verb form (*você chegou*, *a senhora trouxe*, *o senhor quer*), so changing politeness level never requires a new verb ending.
